title: Finite-type flatness gives a finitely presented etale neighborhood
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] of finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and let $x\in X$ with $s=f(x)$ such that $\mathcal F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Then there are an elementary etale neighbourhood $(S',s')\to(S,s)$ (an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] inducing an isomorphism $\kappa(s)\cong\kappa(s')$ of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]) and an open subscheme $V\subset X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{S',s'})$ [def-pc-fibre-product; def-weil-open-immersion] containing the unique point $x'$ over $x$ such that the pullback of $\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] to $V$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] and flat over $\mathcal O_{S',s'}$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over].

source.place: Tag 05I6, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, first proof (affine reduction and induction).

proof.text: Restrict to affine neighbourhoods of $x,s$. If $(\mathcal F_s)_x=0$, Nakayama over $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with ideal $\mathfrak m_s\mathcal O_{X,x}$ gives $\mathcal F_x=0$; the surjective-on-stalk lemma applied to $0\to\mathcal F$ makes $\mathcal F=0$ near $x$, so the identity base change works. Otherwise the affine fibre is finite type over $\kappa(s)$ and hence finite dimensional. Its closed support has finite dimension, so use strong induction on $n=\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)\geq0$, for all such affine data.

Apply localized devissage to obtain $A$ local, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ smooth with geometrically integral fibres of dimension $n$, the finite module $N$, and its marked prime $\mathfrak q$. The initial flatness hypothesis gives $N_{\mathfrak q}$ flat over $A$. Retain the neighbourhood equivalences after further elementary etale local changes supplied by that lemma.

Apply the generic-free-cokernel lemma to $A\to B,N,\mathfrak q$. It supplies $0\to B^r\xrightarrow{\alpha}N\to Q\to0$, with $\alpha$ universally injective, $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ flat, and closed-fibre support of $Q$ either empty or of dimension $<n$. For every test module $M$ in the cokernel-induction lemma, $\widetilde M$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is $A$-flat, and its nonempty closed-fibre support has dimension at $\mathfrak q$ strictly less than $n$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is smooth, it is locally finitely presented. Thus the strong induction hypothesis, quantified over all affine data, supplies exactly that lemma's smaller-support hypothesis. That lemma gives an elementary etale local base $A'$ and $D(g)$ where $\widetilde N$ is finitely presented and flat. For $n=0$, the cokernel has empty fibre support, so the lemma uses its zero-cokernel case and needs no induction hypothesis.

Use the devissage neighbourhood equivalences over $A'$ and intersect the resulting finite-presentation and flat opens. To apply tower realization, set $A_0=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and $U_1=S_1\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ with its marked point; its local ring is $A$. Set $U_2=T$ from step 3, so its marked local ring is $A'$. Both maps are affine etale of finite presentation and preserve the marked residue field. Tower realization gives one elementary etale $(S',s')\to(S,s)$ with $\mathcal O_{S',s'}\cong A'$ over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$. Transport the open and its module along this structural isomorphism. The lemma identifies its fibre over $x$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$, giving the required unique point and the conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_type_flat_etale_neighborhood {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (F : X.Modules) (hF : Scheme.Modules.IsQuasiCoherentFiniteType F) (x : X) (hflat : moduleFlatAt f F x) : ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (s' : S') (e : S' ⟶ S), Etale e ∧ e s' = f x ∧ IsIso (e.residueFieldMap s') ∧ ∃ (V : (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback f (Scheme.fromSpecStalk S' s' ≫ e)).Opens) (x' : V), (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst f (Scheme.fromSpecStalk S' s' ≫ e)) (V.ι x') = x ∧ (V.ι ≫ CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd f (Scheme.fromSpecStalk S' s' ≫ e)) x' = IsLocalRing.closedPoint (S'.presheaf.stalk s') ∧ SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst f (Scheme.fromSpecStalk S' s' ≫ e))).obj F)) ∧ (∀ y : ↥(CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback f (Scheme.fromSpecStalk S' s' ≫ e)), (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst f (Scheme.fromSpecStalk S' s' ≫ e)) y = x → y = V.ι x') ∧ Scheme.Modules.IsFlatOver ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst f (Scheme.fromSpecStalk S' s' ≫ e))).obj F)) (V.ι ≫ CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd f (Scheme.fromSpecStalk S' s' ≫ e))
